OpenAI did not say where its Google number comes from.

paragraphs.text: OpenAI says the number of searches people run in ChatGPT has grown to roughly one fifth of Google's search volume. Adam Fry, who leads the consumer ChatGPT product, shared the figure during a short fireside chat at an OpenAI dinner in New York City on the night of November 2, 2026, according to Big Technology and 9to5Google.

The comparison arrives about two years after OpenAI added web search to ChatGPT, a feature that 9to5Google first reported on October 31, 2024. It is the most direct claim OpenAI has made so far about how its chatbot stacks up against the world's largest search engine.

OpenAI uses a broad definition. Each time a user asks ChatGPT a question and the assistant goes out to search the web, the company counts that as a search, 9to5Google reported. That differs from a traditional search engine, where a search is usually a query typed into a box and answered with a page of links.

9to5Google also pointed out that OpenAI did not disclose where its figure for Google's query volume comes from. Without that number, the one fifth ratio cannot be checked independently, and the outlet said the comparison leaves wide room for interpretation.

For context, 9to5Google described Microsoft's Bing as a distant competitor to Google that has held a single digit share of the search market at any given time. Big Technology's Alex Kantrowitz offered his own rough comparison in the same report, noting that his estimate for Bing's share is his figure and not one OpenAI provided.

Fry gave several other usage figures at the dinner, according to Big Technology. He said ChatGPT went from 1 billion to 1.2 billion weekly active users in 60 days, adding about 200 million people in two months. He said users now create 1.5 billion images a week with the product.

Fry also said about 250 million people use dictation and voice mode in ChatGPT each week, combined. OpenAI passed 50 million paid subscriptions several months ago and has kept growing since then, he said, and its advertising business reached more than $1 billion in annual recurring revenue within 200 days of launching.

On ads, Fry said most people do not seem to mind them in ChatGPT, according to remarks first reported by The Verge and cited by 9to5Google. He also said users value how well ChatGPT personalizes its answers.

Fry used the same appearance to discuss product plans. He said users find the choice between the Chat and Work modes in ChatGPT confusing and that OpenAI plans to bring them together so a single interface decides whether a request is a conversation or a task, Big Technology reported. Asked about timing, he said only that it is coming soon.

The claim lands as Google reshapes its own search product around AI. 9to5Google noted that Google has acknowledged lower monetization tied to its AI search push and has been adding more AI features to Search, a shift the outlet described as at least partly a response to ChatGPT's growth.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the headline ratio matters less than the direction it signals. Because OpenAI counts any web lookup inside a conversation and has not shown its Google baseline, the figure is best treated as a company claim rather than a market share measurement. Still, even a loose one fifth would make ChatGPT a far larger search rival than Bing has been, and the user, image and advertising numbers show a product that is growing on several fronts at once.
The next thing to watch is whether OpenAI or an independent analytics firm publishes the underlying query counts, and whether Google answers with figures of its own in its next earnings report.
